text:
jordan_support: customer reports embeddings usage chart in Console showing unit label \"tokens\" but the numbers look like vectors and are roughly 2x expected. customer provided screenshot: https://acme.screens/abc123 and example time range 2026-03-01..2026-03-07. ticket SUP-4821.

sarah_data: can you paste the org id + a sample request id? :eyes:

jordan_support: org = acme-inc (acct 12345). sample request_id = rq_20260303_9cbf.

sarah_data: thanks. ran a quick query against embeddings_events:
```sql
SELECT day, metric_type, SUM(value) as total
FROM embeddings_events
WHERE org_id = 12345 AND day BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-07'
GROUP BY day, metric_type;
```
I see both `embedding_vectors` and `embedding_token_count` but `embedding_vectors` totals are ~2x the expected and there are duplicates with identical request_id repeated.

mike_enginfra: hmm that rings a bell — we had a replay/consumer offset reset on 2026-03-03 during the kafka migration. We replayed a batch and a dedupe key was incorrect. The consumer used `request_id` only; replays included the same request_id in multiple batches so duplicates passed filtering.

olivia_product: also noticed the Console legend currently maps the plotted series to the token metric name in the UI text. So customers see \"tokens\" but the backend is showing vectors. UI + data mismatch = confusing.

sarah_data: proposed remediation:
- infra: patch consumer dedupe key to `request_id || batch_id` and deploy (prevents future dupes)
- infra: run a backfill to dedupe 2026-03-01..2026-03-07 and re-roll up the daily counts
- frontend: correct legend text to explicitly say \"embedding vectors (count)\" and add tooltip clarifying units vs tokens
Backfill example (sketch):
```sql
INSERT INTO rollups.day_embeddings (org_id, day, metric, value)
SELECT org_id, day, 'embedding_vectors', SUM(DISTINCT request_id || '-' || batch_id)
FROM raw_embeddings_events
WHERE day BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-07' AND org_id = 12345
GROUP BY org_id, day;
```
This will re-aggregate using the proper dedupe key.

mike_enginfra: i'll implement the consumer patch now and run a targeted backfill for acct 12345. ETA ~8 hours for fix + data job (includes validation). tagging oncall.

deploy-bot: deploy started: consumer-dedupe-v2 -> staging (ci/4567) :rocket:

jordan_support: customer escalated to P2 asking for ETA and a short explanation. can we give a public-friendly root cause?

mike_enginfra: short RC: duplicate ingestion from a replayed kafka batch + UI labeling ambiguity. Action items + ETA as above. I'll provide job ids when backfill starts.

olivia_product: i'll submit a small frontend patch to update legend text + tooltip, and add an internal note to the metrics docs about the difference between vectors and tokens.

sarah_data: triage summary for SUP-4821: root cause = (1) replayed events were not deduped due to incomplete dedupe key, (2) Console legend mapped to the wrong metric name. Actions = consumer fix (mike), backfill job (mike + data), frontend label fix (olivia), support comms update (jordan).

mike_enginfra: patch deployed to prod and starting backfill job bf-2026-03-03-acme (job id bf-2026-03-03-01). Monitoring progress.

sarah_data: backfill completed and rollups re-calculated. Sample checks: request_id rq_20260303_9cbf only appears once now and daily totals match expected vector counts. putting validation gist here: https://gist.github.com/redwood/val-4821

jordan_support: confirmed with customer that numbers in Console are now matching their internal totals. customer closed escalation and thanked us. updating SUP-4821 with postmortem notes and closing. :tada:

mike_enginfra: leaving a follow-up ticket to add unit tests around replay dedupe and to add an automated alert if `embedding_vectors` > 1.5x `embedding_token_count` for a daily window.

olivia_product: frontend patch merged and will be in next release, also added tooltip copy: \"Units = embedding vectors. Token counts are available under Token Billing.\"

jordan_support: great work team, thanks for the fast turnaround. closing thread. :pray:
